title: "Encoder"
description: "A model component that transforms input data into a representation for later processing."
term: "Encoder"

difficulty: "Intermediate"

## Simple explanation

An encoder transforms input into a representation that another component
can use. It may convert text, images, or other data into features,
compressed codes, or contextual vectors.

## Technical explanation

An encoder is a learned function mapping input $x$ to representation
$z=f(x)$. In encoder-decoder architectures, the encoder produces features
that condition a decoder. Encoder-only models produce representations
directly, while some architectures combine encoded states with
autoregressive generation.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Encoders are used for classification, retrieval, feature extraction, and
conditional generation. Their representations determine what information
is available to downstream components and may impose bottlenecks or
domain-specific assumptions.

## How it works

The input is tokenized, normalized, or otherwise represented and passed
through layers that transform it into one or more feature vectors. The
architecture and training objective determine whether those vectors
capture local patterns, global context, or task-specific information.

## Practical example

A text encoder can convert a sentence into a vector used to compare it
with other sentences in a semantic search system.

## Common misconceptions

- An encoder does not necessarily compress its input to a smaller
  representation.
- The representation is not automatically interpretable.
- Encoder and decoder are architectural roles; a model may contain one,
  both, or neither as separate components.
